summary: In 1933-34 a group of wealthy US financiers tried to recruit retired Marine general Smedley Butler to lead a veterans' army in a fascist takeover of Roosevelt's government; Butler exposed the plot to Congress, but no one was prosecuted.

evidence.note: Butler enlists in the Marines at 16 during the Spanish-American War, start of his career segment
Butler's service in the Banana Wars, Mexico and Haiti framed as imperial muscle for business
Mussolini bribes US journalists; Hearst syndicate spreads fascist propaganda
Plotters' first ask is a pro-gold-standard speech at the Legion convention
August 1934 meeting where the veterans' army and assistant-president scheme is pitched
Butler testifies to the House committee in November 1934
Hearst papers and the New York Times mock Butler as a crank
Aftermath: War Is a Racket in 1935, Butler votes socialist in 1936

notes: Transcript spells the go-between McGuire; standard spelling is MacGuire. Butler's foreign postings (Cuba, Philippines, China, Honduras, Mexico, Haiti) total only a few minutes of quick biography, so setting is US only. Covered span starts at Butler's 1898 enlistment rather than his 1881 birth, which is a one-line mention.
